name: Kottarakkara Sree Mahaganapathi Kshethram
tagline: Historic Shiva shrine famous for its Ganapathy sub-shrine, unniyappam and temple-astrology traditions
summary: Centuries‑old temple in Kottarakkara (Kollam) whose Shiva shrine is best known for the Mahaganapathy sub‑sanctum, the town's unniyappam offering and living ties to Kerala tantric and temple‑astrology…
description: Kottarakkara Sree Mahaganapathi Kshethram is a historic temple in Kottarakkara town (Kollam district). The principal sanctum is Shiva, but the site is famed across Kerala for its Mahaganapathy (Ganesha) shrine, the unniyappam prasadam and long ritual traditions.

The temple sits at the heart of Kottarakkara's cultural memory: local tradition links the shrine and its craftsmen (Perumthachan legends) to the carving of the Ganapathy idol, and the town is also celebrated as the place where Ramanattam — the ancestor of Kathakali — took shape under the Kottarakkara Thampuran.

Beyond performances and prasadam, the temple participates in Kerala’s living tantric and temple‑astrology world: large temples here observe specialised homams, Udayasthamana pooja rhythms, and the same regionally specific horary practices (devaprasna / Ashtamangala prasna) that guide ritual decisions at many Kerala shrines.

Visitors gain darshan of both Shiva and the popular Ganapathy sub‑shrine, can buy the famed unniyappam prasadam (check the event calendar for Udayasthamana days), and witness temple architecture, the large rectangular temple tank and festival processions when the utsavam is held.
highlights: Mahaganapathy sub‑shrine and the Kottarakkara unniyappam prasadam
Historic link to Ramanattam/Kathakali and the Kottarakkara Thampuran
Daily homams and an organised ritual schedule (see temple timings)
Large rectangular temple tank and timber‑roof Kerala architecture
Witness local tantric/astrological customs during festival seasons

sections.heading: Background
body: The temple complex places Lord Shiva in the main sanctum with a widely revered Mahaganapathy sub‑shrine; the Ganapathy identity and the town’s famous unniyappam offering are inseparable in local memory. The temple website and local guides present the Perumthachan legend about the sculptor who consecrated the Ganapathy idol as tradition, not historical fact.

Kottarakkara town itself is a named birthplace of Ramanattam — an early, vernacular Ramayana stage cycle attributed to Kottarakkara Thampuran in the 17th century — from which Kathakali later evolves. The temple and the town share that cultural association and host related memorials and performances.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Take darshan in the Shiva sanctum and visit the Mahaganapathy shrine; buy or taste the temple unniyappam, the signature prasadam associated with Kottarakkara (note: unniyappam is not available on Udayasthamana Pooja days).

Observe routine rites: the temple publishes a detailed daily puja timetable (morning abhishekam, Ashtadravya Ganapathy homam and evening deeparadhana). During utsavam and festival days you can see decorated processions, elephant and percussion ensembles typical of Kerala temple culture.

If your interest is in ritual culture, ask locally about scheduled Devaprasna / Ashtamangala sessions and homams: these are the Kerala forms of temple horary/astrology and tantric consultation used at many major shrines to settle ritual, structural or community questions (the practice is regional and specialist; public observation varies by temple and event).

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: The shrine sits in central Kottarakkara; darshan and routine pujas follow a published timetable (see the temple timings page). The temple publishes an event calendar and occasional programme notices for the annual utsavam — check the temple website before you travel.

Practical points: photography is commonly restricted inside the sanctum; unniyappam and other offerings may be unavailable on special ritual days; the temple now lists online booking for certain poojas via the Travancore Devaswom Board portal (confirm and book through official channels).

latest.text: Temple website notes online booking for poojas and offerings is available through the Travancore Devaswom Board portal (onlinetdb.com); check the temple event calendar before visiting.
Temple published the Thiruvutsavam (Meda Thiruvathira) 2026 programme notice (utsavam programme and aarattu dates).

visitorInfo.bestTime: Festival season for atmosphere (utsavam dates) or winter months (November–February) for cooler weather.
visitorInfo.howToReach: Kottarakkara town on MC Road (central Kollam district). Nearest railway: Kottarakkara station (Kollam–Sengottai line); Trivandrum International Airport ≈ 80 km south. The temple lies in the town centre — ask locally for the Ganapathi temple or follow signs to the temple tank.
etiquette: Check the temple event calendar and Udayasthamana Pooja dates before you go — unniyappam offering is not served on those days.
If you want to witness ritual/astrological ceremonies (devaprasna, homams), contact the temple office or use the official booking portal to confirm public access.
Respect sanctum restrictions: photography is often limited and certain areas are reserved for priests; dress modestly and follow local guidance.
Use the official Travancore Devaswom Board online booking (onlinetdb.com) for paid poojas rather than third‑party booking sites.
